title: Dedicated fleet capacity economizer and SLO-guided resizer
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a new component and workflow — the Capacity Economizer — that computes conservative, SLO-aware capacity reductions and growth recommendations for dedicated GPU fleets. The goal is to reduce committed spend while keeping throughput and 99th/95th latency SLOs intact. Output recommendations should be explainable, simulator-backed, and actionable from the Console (proposal + apply).
background: Existing fleet recommendations are either static or purely utilization-based and do not account for tail latency, KV cache hit patterns, or model-specific throughput variance. Customers frequently over-provision to protect SLAs. We need an advisor that reasons about token-level cost, request distributions, burst tolerance, and autoscaler hysteresis to safely reclaim capacity or suggest targeted increases.
scope: Produce: (1) offline advisor service that ingests historical telemetry (per-model QPS, latency percentiles, seq length distribution, cache hit rates, GPU utilization), (2) simulator that projects SLO risk and cost delta for a proposed capacity change, (3) Console integration to preview and apply recommendations, and (4) telemetry/alerting hooks to monitor post-apply regressions.
proposed_solution: 1) Build a Capacity Economizer microservice that runs nightly jobs to generate candidate actions: shard consolidation, slab downscale, eviction of underutilized pools, or targeted commit increases for high-queue pools. 2) Use percentile-based SLO model (95th & 99th) with additive safety buffer derived from recent tail variance. 3) Simulate request routing and autoscaler behavior for candidate actions to estimate cost savings and SLO breach probability. 4) Present ranked recommendations in Console with expected monthly savings, confidence score, testable staging apply, and rollback controls.
tradeoffs:
- Conservative recommendations may under-capture savings; aggressive recommendations risk SLA regression.
- Simulation increases compute cost for analysis jobs.
- Tight coupling to historical telemetry means cold-start clusters have less accurate recommendations.
- Some per-customer heuristics will be required; one-size-fits-all models will misclassify atypical workloads.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Economizer produces recommendations for at least 80% of active dedicated pools nightly.
2) Simulator exposes an estimated delta: cost change (USD/mo), expected throughput change, and SLO breach probability for 95th/99th latencies.
3) Console shows recommendations with a single-click to run a staging apply and a clear rollback path.
4) Post-apply monitoring detects regressions and auto-opens an incident/ticket if SLO breach probability materializes.
5) Demonstrated customer POC: one enterprise customer reduced committed capacity by >=15% with no SLO regression over a 7-day canary.
implementation_steps: Define telemetry schema and query set (QPS, per-model p95/p99, GPU util, KV cache hit, queue length)
Prototype economizer logic (heuristic + statistical delta) and run on a 30-day window in dev account
Build simulator that replays sampled traces through autoscaler/resizing logic
API: recommendations endpoint + apply/staging endpoints with audit logs
Console: recommendations dashboard with compare view and deploy button
Integrate alerting: regressions, low-confidence recommendations, failed applies
Run POC with 2 internal beta customers and iterate
qa_tests: Unit tests for economizer heuristics and safety buffer math
Simulator integration tests that assert conservative SLO estimates on synthetic traces
E2E staging apply on non-production pools with monitoring and auto-rollback
Load test: run economizer at scale across 1k pools within nightly SLA
rollback_plan: Every apply creates a rollback snapshot (previous commit and autoscaler parameters). If p95/p99 latency exceeds configured thresholds inside 30 minutes post-apply, automation reverses the change and alerts the SRE/owner. Manual rollback via Console is available with one-click revert.
updates: 2026-02-22: Kickoff meeting with PM, SRE, Console; agreed nightly cadence and SLO targets.
2026-02-28: Telemetry schema finalized; added KV cache hit and per-model seq histograms to job payload.
2026-03-05: Prototype economizer produced stable candidate list for dev pools; observed conservative bias ~18% under true optimal.
2026-03-09: Simulator MVP validated against replayed traces from two dedicated customers; p95 predictions within 12% error margin.
2026-03-12: Console mockups approved by Design; started Console integration tickets.
review_feedback: PM Lina: prefer explicit confidence bands and 'do not touch' tags for compliance-bound pools.
SRE Omar: require automated rollback within 30 minutes and an audit trail for each apply.
Design Priya: show both cost delta and SLO risk in same row for quick decisioning; add explainer modal.
notes: We should plan for a follow-up feature that offers continuous micro-adjustments (hourly) for bursty customers once the nightly pipeline is proven. Consider partnering with Optimize team for model-driven recommendations later.
final_comment: Goal is low-friction, explainable capacity reductions that drive measurable cost savings without surprising regressions. Next milestone: demo POC to two beta customers by 2026-03-25.
